description: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said in remarks made public Sunday that wartime elections would be a "tsunami" that would "destroy the country".  Kyiv has been engulfed in a political crisis over the summer, triggered when Zelensky fired popular defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov, who days later called to organise a vote.

title: DR Congo, AFC/M23 group agree on roadmap for peace negotiations after Swiss talks
description: Mediators representing the Rwanda-backed AFC/M23 armed group and the Democratic Republic of Congo in a joint statement published Sunday said they have agreed on a roadmap for peace talks. The two sides said they had "agreed on the importance of a standardised method for reporting allegations of ceasefire violations".

title: Humanoid robots break human records at World Robot Games in Beijing
description: Humanoid robots smashed sprinting records and competed in boxing, football and martial arts at Beijing’s World Robot Games. While some machines stumbled, toppled or failed to start, the robo-athletes drew cheers from hundreds of spectators and showcased China’s growing dominance in humanoid robotics.

title: French holidaymakers head north to enjoy cooler destinations
description: The summer holidays in France are continuing. However, as we head towards the end of August, a trend has emerged. Destinations in the north of the country are proving more popular, due to the series of heatwaves the country has experienced this year.

title: Saudi Arabia asserts its dominance over Esports as MBS arrives in Paris for 'World Cup'
description:
<![CDATA[
Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman arrives in France for a two-day visit this Sunday. President Emmanuel Macron is hosting the crown prince for the closing ceremony of the so-called Esports World Cup in Paris… which is organised and financed by the Saudis. Analysis by Andy Miah, chair of Sciences Communication & Future Media at the University of Salford.
]]>

title: Presidential campaign heats up in Brazil, as Lula and F. Bolsonaro hold rival rallies
description: Brazilian president Lula de Silva and his political opponent Flavio Bolsonaro pressed on with their presidential campaigns over the weekend, as both candidates held rallies in Rio De Janeiro. Top of the agenda for both candidates was crime, though the two took distinctly different approaches to the issue. Details by Camille Corcoran.

title: Hundreds of Gaza children join a mass swimming lesson to cope with trauma
description: In Gaza, the war has upended the lives of an entire generation of children. In an effort to help them cope with the trauma of the conflict, an NGO has launched a project in Khan Younis: a huge swimming lesson that could even set a world record. Hundreds of children have gathered on the beach to learn how to swim. Story by Charlotte Hughes.

title: Venezuela: Two months after the quake, 12,500 people still live in temporary camps
description: Two months after two earthquakes struck Venezuela, more than 12,500 people are still living in temporary camps in La Guaira. Many survivors are still struggling to come to terms with the loss of loved ones and their homes. They have been forced to adapt to precarious living conditions, exposed to the elements, with little access to medical care and humanitarian aid. France 24 reporters Herminia Fernández and Julio Uribarris visited three camps housing earthquake survivors.

title: Why Saudi Arabia is spending billions to become a global Esports power?
description: Saudi Arabia is betting big on the global gaming industry. It's already gobbled up Electronic Arts in a $55 billion deal and the flagship Esports World Cup is now being held outside the country -- in Paris -- for the first time. This is part of efforts to diversify away from its oil and gas driven economy.

title: Middle East live: Iran's president says country facing 'many problems' as US sanctions loom
description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Sunday said that his country was facing "many problems" and that authorities were striving "to overcome inflation, livelihood problems, unemployment, and to secure the future of the people". His comments came after the US vowed last week to bring about the "collapse" of the regime through a newly announced sanctions campaign. Follow our liveblog fot the latest updates.

title: Ukraine: Zelensky asks for more Patriot interceptors as civilian deaths hit highest level since 2022
description: Kryvyi Rih is still digging through the wreckage. The Russian strike on a shopping centre there, in President Zelensky's own hometown, has now claimed at least sixteen lives, with several people still unaccounted for. It has added urgency to the request Zelensky has been making for months: he needs Patriot interceptors as the threat of winter looms. Camille Knight has more.

title: South Korea tests Arctic route with a first container shipped to Europe
description: Reaching Europe from Asia via the Arctic is nothing new... Russia and China have used this route for years. But yesterday, South Korea sent its first container ship along this path to avoid the traffic blockade in the Middle East. Experts warn the shift could further accelerate the melting of polar ice.

title: US-Canada trade dispute escalates after Carney announces retaliatory tariffs
description: Canada and the US were closing in on a trade deal earlier this week until the negotiations fell apart. Both sides blame each other for last-minute changes to the terms. Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney has announced retaliatory tariffs on the United States after Washington imposed a 50 percent levy on 20-billion-dollars worth of Canadian goods. On Saturday, he addressed the nation for the first time since the talks collapsed, as Charlotte Lam explains.

title: Iran escalates threats as US pushes economic isolation
description: Tensions between Iran and the United States continue to escalate. Tehran is threatening to regard as enemies any countries that join the US sanctions, in response to Washington’s calls to isolate its economy. A press conference is scheduled for Monday to outline the US strategy. Story by Camille Corcoran.

title: Trump says Canada wants 'benefits of being a State, without being one' as trade war deepens
description: US President Donald Trump slammed Canada on Sunday, saying the country wanted "the benefits of being a State, without being one", in response to Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announcing retaliatory tariffs following failed trade negotiations.

title: Macron hosts Saudi crown prince for two-day visit to include issues from energy to Mideast
description: Saudi crown prince and de facto ruler Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) was welcomed on Sunday by French President Emmanuel Macron for a two-day visit to the country. Several agreements on health, transport and energy will be signed on the second day of the visit on Monday underlining the strength of the Paris-Riyadh relationship.

title: Togo says it has 'serious' evidence against detained French filmmakers
description: Togo’s government said Saturday it had “serious and corroborative evidence” against two French documentary filmmakers arrested last month alongside their Togolese fixer. The three men deny charges of making “false declarations”.

title: Fontainebleau forest near Paris reopens after devastating wildfire
description: Fontainebleau forest reopened to the public Saturday, with 80 percent of the popular Paris-area nature reserve accessible again after a wildfire scorched around 2,000 hectares last month. A fifth of the forest remains closed because of safety risks.

title: US deports 20 people to Liberia, the first of 1,200 migrants under Trump deal
description: <p>Agreement is among largest third-country deportations driven by Trump administration’s immigration crackdown </p><p>Twenty deportees from the United States arrived in Liberia on Thursday, as part of a new agreement that will see the west African country receive as many as 1,200 people under the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/trump-administration">Trump administration</a>’s immigration crackdown.</p><p>The group arrived at the Roberts international airport outside the capital, Monrovia. The Liberia-US agreement is one of the largest third-country deportation arrangements pursued by the administration since Trump returned to office last year.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/20/liberia-deportation-agreement">Continue reading...</a>

title: More than 100 dead after goldmine collapses in Central African Republic
description: <p>The collapse was caused by a landslide, while local officials say the death toll is likely to rise as recovery efforts continue</p><p>More than 100 people have died after an artisanal goldmine at a small village in western Central African Republic (CAR) caved in due to a landslide, local officials and aid workers said on Wednesday.</p><p>The landslide happened on Tuesday afternoon in the village of Zamboye, about 50km (31 miles) from the town of Baboua and close to the border of Cameroon. Footage on social media appeared to show an avalanche of sand descend on a group of people, likely the miners, and cover them.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/20/gold-mine-collapse-deadly-landslide-central-african-republic">Continue reading...</a>

title: Five Americans among seven killed in safari helicopter crash in Kenya
description: <p>Officials say all seven people onboard killed, including Telemundo executive and Ecuador intelligence chief</p><p>Seven people, including five Americans, were killed when a safari helicopter crashed on Wednesday morning in a remote part of northern Kenya, according to local police and the state department.</p><p>Among the dead were an executive with Telemundo, the US-based Spanish-language network owned by NBC Universal, and the director of Ecuador’s national intelligence service.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/19/kenya-helicopter-safari-crash">Continue reading...</a>

title: Spain to allow 500 children in Ceuta to go to mainland in immigration U-turn
description: <p>Madrid government changes stance after previously saying anyone who entered territory illegally would be sent back</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/aug/19/europe-ukraine-zelenskyy-mykhailo-fedorov-parliament-vote-corruption-probe-russia-belgium-wildfires-latest-news-updates">Europe live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>The Spanish government has U-turned and said it will allow 500 migrant children in Ceuta to relocate to the mainland.</p><p>The majority of the estimated <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/15/moroccan-police-arrest-more-than-100-people-as-they-attempt-to-enter-ceuta">70,000 people who crossed into Ceuta</a> – a Spanish territory on the coast of north Africa – on 30 July have returned to Morocco. However, under Spanish law, the state has a duty of care to young, unaccompanied migrants until they reach the age of 18.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/19/spain-allows-500-migrant-minors-in-ceuta-to-relocate-to-the-mainland-in-u-turn">Continue reading...</a>

title: Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of the Congo now deadliest in country’s history
description: <p>At least 2,325 people have died from the virus, according to official data, with outbreak on track to be biggest in history</p><p>The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is now the deadliest in the country’s history, with at least 2,325 people dead, according to government data, surpassing the toll from the 2018-20 outbreak.</p><p>The DRC’s public health institute said confirmed cases had risen to 4,945, including 101 detected in the previous 24 hours.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/17/ebola-outbreak-drc-democratic-republic-of-congo-deadliest-in-history">Continue reading...</a>

title: ‘No more!!!’: Trump lashes out after US-Canada talks devolve into trade war
description: <p>PM Mark Carney says ‘we got attacked’ as tariffs come into force on items from hockey sticks to tongue depressors</p><p>Donald Trump has hit back at Canada after a breakdown in negotiations <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/22/canada-tariffs-trump-trade-deal-talks-fail">plunged the two countries into a trade war</a>.</p><p>In his first public comments since negotiations collapsed on Friday in Washington, the US president wrote on social media: “Canada wants the benefits of being a State, without being one!!!”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/23/donald-trump-lashes-out-after-us-canada-talks-devolve-into-trade-war">Continue reading...</a>

title: Canada vows ‘dollar for dollar’ response as US puts 50% tariffs on some goods
description: <p>Collapse of trade talks could lead to job losses, but biggest impact on traditional allies is expected to be political </p><p>The US has imposed 50% tariffs on some goods from Canada, and Mark Carney, the country’s prime minister, has vowed to match them “dollar for dollar” after the collapse of trade talks.</p><p>The tariffs came into force on roughly $20bn (£14.6bn) of goods – ranging from hockey sticks to tongue depressors – at 04.00GMT. Trade experts said the tariffs could result in some job losses, but the largest impact is expected to be political, driving a further wedge between the traditional allies.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/22/canada-tariffs-trump-trade-deal-talks-fail">Continue reading...</a>

title: JD Vance reportedly mocks Carney for trying to ‘out-tough’ Trump on trade
description: <p>Audio recording of US vice-president apparently made at New York fundraiser and shared with Canadian Press</p><p>Leaked audio from a private event has reportedly captured the US vice-president, JD Vance, mocking Canada for apparently capitulating in a trade deal and taunting the prime minister, Mark Carney, for trying to “out-tough” Donald Trump.</p><p>The recording, which was reportedly made at a fundraiser and <a href="https://www.thecanadianpressnews.ca/business/vance-weighs-in-on-jivani-trade-advocacy-and-how-carney-tried-to-out-tough-trump/article_a74328a0-9cf8-5047-8da3-2673eb755c4d.html">shared with the Canadian Press</a>, comes in the last stretch of a difficult negotiation in which the US president has threatened to impose 50% tariffs on Canada.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/21/jd-vance-mark-carney-out-tough-trump-trade">Continue reading...</a>

title: Strangers in their own land: Mexicans deported from Trump’s America find refuge in ‘Little LA’
description: <p>With plentiful jobs and community support, one Mexico City neighbourhood has become a haven for those who have lived much of their lives in the US</p><p>With its wide avenues lined with tall palm trees, its quaint cafes and old-school cantinas, as well as the mix of English and Spanish spoken on the street, the Tabacalera neighborhood in downtown Mexico City has a certain US feel – so much so that it is has become known <a href="https://www.wsj.com/video/in-little-la-us-deportees-adjust-to-life-in-mexico/77540AB5-7EC5-421E-8E79-C5CF52FF7F50">as Little LA</a>.</p><p>The nickname is about more than appearances, however. In recent years, this corner of the metropolis has become a haven for many Mexicans deported from the US, particularly those who spent years or decades living across the border and for whom Mexico feels like a foreign country. In Little LA, they have found a more familiar place to belong.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/21/mexico-city-little-la-us-deportees">Continue reading...</a>

title: Adviser to far-right Latin American leaders arrested for allegedly plotting to kill girlfriend
description: <p>Fernando Cerimedo, 42, arrested on suspicion of ordering shooting of Bolivian lawyer Nadia Beller</p><p>A senior adviser to many of Latin America’s new wave of far-right leaders has been arrested for allegedly masterminding the attempted murder of his girlfriend.</p><p>The businessman and political consultant Fernando Cerimedo, 42, had been working as an adviser to the Bolivian president, Rodrigo Paz Pereira, and was one of the main strategists behind Javier Milei’s campaign in Argentina’s 2023 presidential election.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/19/fernando-cerimedo-adviser-far-right-latin-american-leaders-arrested-allegedly-plotting-kill-girlfriend">Continue reading...</a>

title: Man leaves young son on Mount Fuji before ascending Japan’s highest peak
description: <p>Boy, seven, had complained of feeling tired so father left him with snacks and a soft drink and continued his climb</p><p>A man who abandoned his seven-year-old son on Mount Fuji in Japan after the boy complained of feeling tired while on a family hike has been reprimanded by local police.</p><p>A worker on Japan’s highest mountain discovered the child sitting alone on a bench near the sixth station of the Fujinomiya trail at an altitude of more than 2,000 metres (6,500 feet) on Thursday.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/22/man-leaves-young-son-mount-fuji-japan">Continue reading...</a>

title: Tiananmen Square vigil organisers in Hong Kong found guilty of ‘inciting subversion’
description: <p>UK Foreign Office condemns use of national security law to convict activists Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung</p><p>Two Hong Kong activists who organised annual vigils marking China’s deadly Tiananmen crackdown in 1989 have been found guilty of “incitement to subversion” in one of the most high-profile cases in Hong Kong since Beijing imposed its national security law in 2020.</p><p>Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, and Chow Hang-tung, 41, “incited other persons to organise, plan, commit or participate in acts by unlawful means with a view to subverting the state power”, a press summary handed out to reporters said. The defendants each face a maximum penalty of 10 years in jail, with sentencing expected at a later date.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/21/tiananmen-square-vigil-hong-kong-alliance-activists-guilty-verdict-lee-cheuk-yan-chow-hang-tung">Continue reading...</a>

title: Weather tracker: Extreme rain deluges Japan and South Korea
description: <p>Downpours break records and cause transport chaos, evacuations and deaths, as people get trapped inside vehicles </p><p>South Korea and Japan were hit by <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/14/japan-deadly-rain-evacuation-thousands-stranded-tokyo-airport-weather">extreme rain</a> late last week and into this week. On 13 August in the city of Chiba near Tokyo there was a record-breaking 115mm of rainfall in just one hour, while the nearby city of Sakura broke its own record with 97mm in one hour. Local authorities issued a level 5 emergency warning for heavy rain, the highest alert level and the first time one has been issued since the system was implemented in May.</p><p>More than 100,000 households were asked to evacuate, with more than 20,000 in the Chiba prefecture left without power, while thousands of people were stranded at Tokyo’s Narita airport. Thirteen people have been confirmed dead, at least three of whom were found trapped inside their vehicles. One person is still missing.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/aug/21/weather-tracker-extreme-rainfall-japan-south-korea">Continue reading...</a>

title: Russia’s missile tests around disputed islands anger Japan
description: <p>Pacific fleet launched missile drills near what Moscow calls the Kuril Islands but Japan regards as its Northern Territories</p><p>Japan has criticised missile tests carried out by Russia’s navy around the disputed islands visited by Vladimir Putin last week amid continuing tensions between the two countries.</p><p>Russia’s Pacific fleet said on Thursday that it had fired Bastion surface-to-ship missiles from Etorofu, the largest island in the disputed archipelago, simulating an attack on enemy vessels, hitting all of its targets approximately 300km away.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/21/russia-launch-missiles-kuril-islands-japan">Continue reading...</a>

title: Founder of China’s Evergrande jailed for life after pleading guilty to fraud
description: <p>Hui Ka Yan also forfeits all his personal property and the company he set up is given hefty fines</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/live/2026/aug/20/rising-uk-consumer-confidence-economy-andy-burnham-latest-news-updates">Business live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>The founder of Evergrande, one of China’s largest property developers, has been sentenced to life in prison and had all of his personal property confiscated.</p><p>Hui Ka Yan, 67 and once named by Forbes as China’s richest man, with a net worth of $42.5bn (£31.2bn) in 2017, <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/apr/14/china-evergrande-fraud-hui-ka-yan-trial-property">pleaded guilty</a> in April to eight charges.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/aug/20/evergrande-founder-jailed-life-fraud-hui-ka-yan">Continue reading...</a>

title: Swans fans turn up to support women’s team – as it happened
description: <p>This blog is now closed</p><p><strong>Victorian Labor expands on free dental care election promise</strong></p><p>The Victorian premier, <strong>Ben Carroll</strong>, and health minister, <strong>Ingrid Stitt</strong>, have held a press conference this morning off the back of their announcement yesterday that the Labor government would open <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/aug/22/victoria-labor-free-dental-care-ben-carroll-election-promise">10 free public dental clinics if re-elected in November</a>.</p><p>You can’t use a Medicare card for dental unless you’ve got a healthcare card or you are a category of a particular citizen, it is very difficult … I’ve been visiting a lot of dentists over the past few weeks. There [are] waiting lists. People are in enormous, unbearable pain.</p><p>This will be a cost of living measure but it will also make sure that we deal with the healthcare of some of the most vulnerable Victorians. This is really going to fill the gap that’s been there for decades.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/live/2026/aug/23/australia-news-live-anthony-albanese-sydney-swans-police-investigation-alan-jones-antisemitism-inquiry-icac-nsw-liberals-ntwnfb">Continue reading...</a>

title: Liberal plan to split Victorian appeals court attacked as ‘thought bubble’ that would politicise judiciary
description: <p>Opposition leader Jess Wilson says new dedicated court of criminal appeal would set precedents for tougher sentences</p><ul><li><p>Get our <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/email-newsletters?CMP=cvau_sfl">breaking news email</a>, <a href="https://app.adjust.com/w4u7jx3">free app</a> or <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/series/full-story?CMP=cvau_sfl">daily news podcast</a></p></li></ul><p>A radical overhaul of Victoria’s highest court, proposed by the Liberal party to increase sentences, has been criticised by legal and human rights groups who warn it would politicise the judiciary.</p><p>The opposition leader, Jess Wilson, on Sunday announced that if elected in November the Coalition would split the court of appeal in two, creating a dedicated court of criminal appeal alongside a separate court of civil appeal.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/aug/23/victoria-election-liberals-plan-split-appeals-court-attacked-as-thought-bubble-politicise-judiciary">Continue reading...</a>

title: Hanson forced to intervene after One Nation MP says party’s migration target ‘not too different’ from Labor’s
description: <p>David Farley says party wants 100,000 migrant rural workers in addition to the 130,000 migration target it considers the ‘true’ number</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/live/2026/aug/23/australia-news-live-anthony-albanese-sydney-swans-police-investigation-alan-jones-antisemitism-inquiry-icac-nsw-liberals-ntwnfb">Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates</a></p></li><li><p>Get our <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/email-newsletters?CMP=cvau_sfl">breaking news email</a>, <a href="https://app.adjust.com/w4u7jx3">free app</a> or <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/series/full-story?CMP=cvau_sfl">daily news podcast</a></p></li></ul><p>The One Nation MP David Farley says the minor party’s net migration target is “not too different” to Labor’s, forcing his leader to issue an urgent clarification amid rising confusion over the policy.</p><p>It is the second time Pauline Hanson has <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/may/03/barnaby-joyce-blames-campaign-pressure-after-one-nations-farrer-candidates-immigration-slip-up-ntwnfb">had to issue a correction</a> after the member for Farrer seemed to contradict One Nation’s restrictive approach to immigration.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/aug/23/one-nation-mp-david-farley-immigration-target-net-overseas-migration-not-too-different-labor-rural-workforce">Continue reading...</a>

title: Sydney Marathon admits ‘unfortunate error’ as finisher’s medal depicts Munich stadium as race highlight
description: <p>‘Landmarks’ side of the medal features the Allianz Arena in  German city rather than Allianz Stadium in Sydney</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/live/2026/aug/23/australia-news-live-anthony-albanese-sydney-swans-police-investigation-alan-jones-antisemitism-inquiry-icac-nsw-liberals-ntwnfb">Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates</a></p></li><li><p>Get our <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/email-newsletters?CMP=cvau_sfl">breaking news email</a>, <a href="https://app.adjust.com/w4u7jx3">free app</a> or <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/series/full-story?CMP=cvau_sfl">daily news podcast</a></p></li></ul><p>In a week’s time, the proud runners finishing the Sydney Marathon will receive a medal showing the landmarks they have just sped past – plus one they definitely didn’t.</p><p>In what organisers have admitted was an “unfortunate error”, a stadium in Munich, Germany, was erroneously etched on to the event’s participation medal instead of a local Sydney landmark.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/aug/23/sydney-marathon-medal-allianz-stadium-munich-germany-unfortunate-error">Continue reading...</a>

title: Fur seal’s death marks first Australian mainland mammal fatality from spreading H5 bird flu strain
Russia withdraws ambassador to UK as Kremlin raises pressure over Ukraine support
description: <p>Embassy in London says Andrey Kelin left last month after seven years in diplomatic post</p><p>Russia has withdrawn its ambassador to the UK, it has emerged, as the Kremlin continues to try to put pressure on Britain over its support for Ukraine.</p><p>Andrey Kelin left last month after seven years in the diplomatic post, according to the Russian embassy in London.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/23/russia-withdraws-ambassador-uk-kremlin-pressure-ukraine-andrey-kelin">Continue reading...</a>

title: Holding election in wartime would risk destroying Ukraine, says Zelenskyy
description: <p>President sharply criticises proposal, saying ‘elections right now are a tsunami for the state that will split Ukraine’</p><p>Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said holding elections in Ukraine during wartime would risk splitting the country at a time when Russia is amassing ballistic missiles and considering whether to mobilise an extra 300,000 soldiers.</p><p>The Ukrainian president, responding for the first time to <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/18/ukraines-dismissed-defence-minister-calls-for-wartime-presidential-election">a demand made by</a> the sacked former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov, sharply criticised an idea that he said was impractical given Russia appeared to have no interest in a ceasefire.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/23/ukraine-election-wartime-risk-russia-zelenskyy">Continue reading...</a>

title: Pine-cone grenades and planet-baking carbon: the French fires 170 years in the making – a visual guide
description: <p>An 1857 decree to drain swamps and plant a monoculture, detritus from the trees and global heating combined to produce the conditions for the Gironde inferno</p><p>The ruinous fires that overran parts of France this summer have burned more land than ever recorded, forced more people from their homes than at any point since the second world war and caused what scientists suspect is the country’s first firestorm thundercloud. The smoke from France’s biggest inferno in nearly 80 years choked Limoges, a city 125 miles (200km) from the flames, with more toxic dust than Delhi residents inhaled on the city’s worst day of smog last year.</p><p>The blaze that tore through forests outside <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/01/wildfire-france-firefighters-battling-france-megafire">Bordeaux</a> in late July took just a few weeks to reforge France’s relationship with fire, but the conditions behind it were centuries in the making.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/23/french-fires-150-years-in-the-making-visual-guide">Continue reading...</a>

title: The ‘ordinary’ woman accused of assassinating a Russian commander in Crimea
description: <p>Friends close to Margarita Reutt are shocked she could allegedly plant bomb that killed Ukrainian defector Robert Shageev, while others recall a stubborn grit to see any plan through</p><p>It was just after dawn in Sevastopol when a powerful explosion tore through a quiet square in a residential district of the Russian-occupied Crimean port city.</p><p>Hidden inside a rubbish bin, a bomb containing the equivalent of about 500g of TNT detonated on 13 August as Robert Shageev, the deputy commander of a Russian Black Sea fleet submarine brigade, walked past in naval uniform. He was killed on the spot.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/23/ordinary-woman-margarita-reutt-accused-assassinating-russian-commander-crimea">Continue reading...</a>

title: Seventeen-year-old girl killed in sword attack at school in Sweden
description: <p>Three other people wounded after 18-year-old man wielding sword assail students in Fagersta school</p><p>A 17-year-old girl has been killed after a teenager brandishing a sword attacked students at a school in Sweden, police have confirmed.</p><p>Three other people were wounded in the incident during classes in the central town of Fagersta on Friday afternoon, including two boys aged 12 and 17 who sustained minor injuries.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/22/seventeen-year-old-girl-killed-in-sword-attack-at-school-in-sweden">Continue reading...</a>

title: Iran-linked hackers blamed for cyber-attack that shut down UK power plant
description: <p>Incident marks apparent escalation by Tehran in its in retaliation against UK over allowing US to use British bases</p><p>Hackers linked to Iran have been blamed for a cyber-attack that caused a British power plant to be temporarily shut down.</p><p>The incident involved a small-scale energy generator, according to the UK government, which said that at no point was there a risk to the wider energy system.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/23/iran-linked-hackers-blamed-cyber-attack-british-power-plant">Continue reading...</a>

title: Iran’s foreign minister calls threat of new US economic sanctions ‘desperate’
description: <p>Abbas Araghchi says country is unbowed but president Masoud Pezeshkian admits its people face ‘many problems’</p><p>Iran’s foreign minister has dismissed the threat of a fresh round of US economic sanctions as a “desperate” ploy, even as its president acknowledged that the Iranian people are facing “many problems” amid Washington’s efforts to isolate and debilitate the country’s economy.</p><p>Last week, Donald Trump announced <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/20/trump-threatens-crush-iran-economy-war-hormuz">a new campaign to increase the pressure on the Iranian economy</a>, calling it “the most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country”. The US Treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, is expected to announce further punitive economic measures on Iran – which he has described as “the toughest sanctions in history” – on Monday.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/23/iran-new-security-chief-trump-economic-war-enemies-mohsen-rezaei">Continue reading...</a>

title: Burnham to face pressure at Labour conference to recognise Israel’s actions in Gaza as genocide
description: <p>Grassroots groups to urge PM to break with Starmer policy and impose full arms embargo on Israel</p><p>Grassroots Labour groups are gearing up for a conference showdown with Andy Burnham over Gaza, as the party’s members seek to force the prime minister to recognise Israel’s actions as a genocide and impose a full arms embargo.</p><p>Momentum, Labour &amp; Palestine, the Campaign for Labour Party Democracy and Palestine Solidarity Campaign (PSC) plan to ramp up pressure on Burnham before his first Labour conference as prime minister next month.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/aug/23/andy-burnham-pressure-labour-conference-recognise-israel-actions-gaza-genocide">Continue reading...</a>

title: Israeli settler attacks shift focus to West Bank areas under direct Palestinian rule
description: <p>Report says violence is moving from Israeli-controlled areas to those earmarked for a future Palestinian state</p><p>Violent Israeli settler attacks in the two areas of the occupied West Bank under direct Palestinian rule have almost doubled since 2025, as settlers pursue a self-proclaimed “great settlement revolution” in the very heart of the territory earmarked for a Palestinian state.</p><p>According to a <a href="https://www.yesh-din.org/en/the-next-frontier_eng">report by the Israeli human rights organisation Yesh Din</a>, shared with the Guardian, data shows that almost two-thirds of incidents of settler violence so far in 2026 have taken place in the so-called Areas A and B – placed under Palestinian Authority governance in the 1995 Oslo accords.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/21/israeli-settler-attacks-shift-to-heart-of-territory-earmarked-for-palestinian-state">Continue reading...</a>

title: Israel admits its soldiers fired at car in which Hind Rajab was killed
description: <p>Military orders criminal investigation into deaths of five-year-old and six family members in Gaza in 2024</p><p>The Israeli military admitted on Wednesday its troops had opened fire on a car carrying five-year-old Hind Rajab and six family members in Gaza in 2024, saying it had ordered a criminal investigation into the killing.</p><p>The killing of Hind and her family was one of the most high profile of a series of incidents involving civilian casualties during the first months of the Gaza conflict which prompted international outrage.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/19/israel-admits-it-soldiers-fired-at-car-in-which-hind-rajab-was-killed">Continue reading...</a>

title: Jailed ex-Pakistan PM Imran Khan allowed brief hospital visit after uproar over health
description:
<p>Supreme court ordered transfer of ex-leader whose health is reportedly deteriorating, but he was returned to prison several hours later</p><p><br>
 Pakistan’s jailed former prime minister <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/imran-khan">Imran Khan</a> was briefly taken to a hospital in the country’s capital on supreme court orders after weeks of uproar about his deteriorating health.</p><p>Khan, 73, was transferred to the hospital in the early hours of Friday, but then moved back to Adiala prison in Rawalpindi after a ⁠few hours, a spokesperson for his party said on Friday.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/20/imran-khan-hospital-pakistan">Continue reading...</a>

title: Taliban threaten former Afghan police worker after MoD leak reveals identity
description: <p>UK has refused resettlement application despite ‘years of loyal service’ that have resulted in ‘constant fear’ of reprisals</p><p>A man has received threats from the Taliban after his work for the Afghan police was revealed by a Ministry of Defence leak and the UK refused his application for resettlement.</p><p>Hamid* worked for the Afghan national police special unit and received certificates for his work signed by senior British figures praising his “dedication, unparalleled service and leadership”. His details were also included in an <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2025/jul/15/afghan-resettlement-scheme-secret-superinjunction-explainer">accidental 2022 leak</a> by an MoD official that identified 18,700 Afghans who had worked with or for the British government.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/16/taliban-threaten-former-afghan-police-worker-after-mod-leak-reveals-identity">Continue reading...</a>

title: Concerns grow over increased global ties with Taliban in Afghanistan
description: <p>Campaigners fear deeper diplomatic contacts are undermining demands for improvements in human rights </p><p>The Taliban in Afghanistan have launched a diplomatic effort to end their isolation as major regional and international powers show a readiness to engage more closely with the repressive regime despite its systematic human rights abuses.</p><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/aug/04/five-years-taliban-rule-afghan-women-and-girls-need-our-help">Five years after the Taliban took power</a>, an increasing number of countries are renewing ties or scaling up diplomatic contacts with the hardline Islamists, who seized power in Kabul in 2021 after 20 years of brutal insurgent warfare.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/15/concern-grow-global-ties-taliban-afghanistan-human-rights">Continue reading...</a>

title: Ex-Myanmar ambassador to UK on trial for trespassing in diplomatic residence
description: <p>Kyaw Zwar Minn was ousted for declaring loyalty to Aung San Suu Kyi after 2021 coup but refused to leave his home</p><p>Myanmar’s ousted ambassador to the UK has gone on trial on trespassing charges for refusing to leave a diplomatic residence after being <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/apr/13/ousted-myanmar-ambassador-says-his-relatives-fear-reprisals-kyaw-zwar-minn">unceremoniously locked out of the embassy</a> in 2021.</p><p>Shortly after Myanmar’s military seized power in 2021, triggering mass protests that spiralled into a civil war, Kyaw Zwar Minn was locked out of the embassy for declaring his loyalty to the deposed civilian leader Aung San Suu Kyi.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/aug/12/ex-myanmar-ambassador-uk-kyaw-zwar-minn-trial-trespassing-diplomatic-residence">Continue reading...</a>

title: The return of the caspian tiger: how a species feared extinct has come back to Kazakhstan
description: <p>The wild capture and release of a female big cat into a nature reserve is the first step towards reintroducing a population that hasn’t been seen for 70 years</p><p>On 31 July, “Umit” – which means hope in Kazakh – was released into a nature reserve on the edge of Lake Balkhash after more than a decade of careful planning to return the caspian tiger to the region. With this release, Kazakhstan became the first country to restore its tiger range after they had been thought extinct, with the last reliable sighting in the country recorded more than 70 years ago.</p><p>Umit – a wild-caught female tiger transported from the Russian far east – will be joined by more big cats in the coming years, with plans to establish a self-sustaining population of about 50. A wild-caught male flown from Russia is still being monitored by authorities and will be released when he is judged fit to survive alone. Two wild tiger cubs are also being reared on the reserve in special enclosures, with as little human contact as possible, and are likely to be released into the marshlands next year, to feast on boar, deer and kulans, a type of wild donkey.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/aug/11/extinction-caspian-tiger-release-female-kazakhstan-aoe">Continue reading...</a>

title: Boys aged 16 and 17 among seven people dead in A66 crash that killed two police officers
description: <p>Tributes paid to Matthew Blades, 37, and Tom Clough, 38, of Cleveland police, who died after collision with car travelling wrong way</p><p></p><p>A 16-year-old boy was one of seven people killed on Teesside when a car travelling the wrong way on the A66, believed to be using cloned plates, crashed head-on into a police vehicle.</p><p>Cole Robert Worthy, 16, Theo Rae, 17, Makai Saddington, 18, and 23-year-olds Michael Robert Cahill and Jacob Matusiak died when their Volkswagen Passat collided with a marked armed response vehicle early on Saturday near Middlesbrough.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/aug/23/tributes-paid-cleveland-police-killed-a66-crash-south-bank">Continue reading...</a>

title: CrossCountry cancels almost all rail services after power cut hits control centre
description: <p>Transport secretary asks ‘publicly owned operators to lay on extra services where possible’</p><p>CrossCountry has cancelled almost all of its train services in Great Britain after a power cut in Birmingham hit its control centre on Sunday.</p><p>Most services have been cancelled until further notice, including routes from Glasgow to Edinburgh, Manchester to Birmingham, Cheltenham to Cardiff and Newcastle to Edinburgh.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/aug/23/crosscountry-cancels-almost-all-rail-services-after-power-cut-hits-control-centre">Continue reading...</a>

title: Burnham stays away from No 10 North wedding after bride’s plea
description: <p>PM sends video message to newlyweds instead after bride Sarah Burwin asked him not to ‘ruin’ vibe at Heron House</p><p>Andy Burnham fulfilled a bride’s wishes by not turning up for her wedding after she asked him not to spoil her big day as she got married at the building housing No 10 North.</p><p>Sarah Burwin had pleaded on TikTok in July for Burnham not to work from the building in Manchester that day, which hosts the government’s northern headquarters and the city’s register office.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/aug/23/burnham-stays-away-from-no-10-north-wedding-after-brides-plea">Continue reading...</a>

title: Manuscript fragments hiding in plain sight shed light on medieval Guernsey’s literary life
description: <p>Researchers say texts from 12th to 15th centuries ‘hint at a culture which has not even been imagined’</p><p>Unprecedented insights into the literary and intellectual life on the island of Guernsey during the middle ages have been revealed through the discovery of 17 medieval manuscript fragments.</p><p>Dating from between the 12th and 15th centuries, they offer evidence of wide-ranging reading tastes, with everything from an extract from a play and an Ovid poem to passages from the Bible and a travel text.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/aug/23/manuscript-fragments-discovery-medieval-guernsey">Continue reading...</a>

title: ‘The line’s running half-empty’: Llanwern steelworks feels the heat from cheap steel imports
description: <p>New quotas to protect UK firms and jobs appear to be having opposite effect in products such as galvanised steel</p><p>At Tata Steel’s factory in Llanwern, south Wales, production lines that should be running full-time are now falling quiet for parts of the day, with workers being put on to maintenance and cleaning work while machines sit idle.</p><p>There aren’t enough orders to keep them running all the time, the company says, because of a surge of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/jun/25/uk-to-halve-tariff-free-steel-imports-to-counter-glut-of-cheap-chinese-metal">cheap steel coming from Asian countries</a> that is threatening the viability of several UK sites that make similar products, and risk hundreds of jobs.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/aug/23/llanwern-steelworks-cheap-steel-imports">Continue reading...</a>

title: Former Abercrombie CEO mentally fit for sex-trafficking trial, judge says
description: <p>Michael Jeffries is ruled mentally competent to stand trial after being hospitalized for months for dementia symptoms</p><p>The former CEO of Abercrombie &amp; Fitch has been ruled mentally competent to stand trial as <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2024/oct/25/former-abercrombie-ceo-mike-jeffries-plea">he faces sex-trafficking charges</a> after being hospitalized for months for dementia and Alzheimer’s symptoms.</p><p>Michael Jeffries, who is 82 and free <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2024/oct/22/former-abercrombie-ceo-arrested-sex-trafficking">on bond</a> for now, is scheduled to be tried in late October, alongside two co-defendants: his partner Matthew Smith and staffer James Jacobson. A pretrial hearing was slated for Thursday.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/23/ex-abercrombie-ceo-mentally-fit-sex-trafficking-trial">Continue reading...</a>

title: Arrest warrant issued for wife of Massachusetts officer found dead at home
description: <p>Woman remains missing more than five days after police found officer she was married to dead in their home</p><p>An arrest warrant has been issued for a mental health advocate who remained missing on Sunday, more than five days after police found the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/massachusetts">Massachusetts</a> officer she had been married to dead in their home.</p><p>Karen Solomon, 58, was last spotted in a doorbell camera video, walking down a street in a T-shirt, shorts and flip-flops early Tuesday morning, just minutes after Worcester police officers responded to a call from the home where Kurt Solomon was found dead.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/23/massachusetts-officer-death-home-wife-arrest-warrant">Continue reading...</a>

title: Double jeopardy? Luigi Mangione state case unlikely to proceed, experts say
description: <p>Defense files motion to dismiss state case after federal guilty plea but prosecutors say they are prepared to litigate</p><p>After Luigi Mangione <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/14/luigi-mangione-hearing-federal-case">admitted</a> in Manhattan federal court that he killed UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, most experts believe that the state murder case against is highly unlikely to proceed – though some still see a slim possibility that it may yet happen.</p><p>Mangione, who <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2026/aug/14/luigi-mangione-court-plea-deal-ceo-killing-live">pleaded guilty</a> on 14 August to two federal stalking counts, was scheduled for a New York state trial on 8 September for murder and weapons charges in the December 2024 killing. In the wake of Mangione’s surprise plea, legal experts said New York’s state-level double jeopardy law – which means someone cannot be tried twice for the same crime – could derail his local prosecution.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/23/luigi-mangione-state-case-brian-thompson">Continue reading...</a>

title: Personal care products are awash in unlabeled toxic chemicals, study finds
description: <p>Even products labeled ‘eco’, ‘green’ or ‘natural’ can contain dangerous compounds including Pfas</p><p>Common personal care products widely contain unlabeled toxic chemicals, results from a <a href="https://pubs.acs.org/ehnea2/article/doi/10.1021/envhealth.6c00181/5252510/Hidden-Hazards-Nontargeted-Chemical-Analysis?_kx=XNWwVJyA8PLpY0aFJp1XnhL1qc4uFux9_6KFyk6kc5Y.TNuYmj">new peer-reviewed study</a> suggest. The testing of more than 110 items ranging from shampoo to baby lotions found evidence of unlabeled toxic chemicals in about 85%.</p><p>Many contained multiple ingredients known to be carcinogens or health hazards, and even 26% of products labeled “eco”, “green” or “natural” contained at least one dangerous compound. The products averaged more than three times as many chemicals than were listed on labels.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/23/personal-care-products-unlabeled-toxic-chemicals">Continue reading...</a>

title: Against the wind: despite Trump’s attacks, unions are fighting for good US clean energy jobs
description: <p>Since Hurricane Sandy in 2012, a growing labor movement has addressed the climate crisis and economic inequality</p><p>Ryan McElroen had spent years repairing the New York City subway underground when he got the opportunity to work in the middle of the ocean.</p><p>“I had no views other than the darkness at work,” he said. “Then I went polar opposite.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/23/wind-energy-unions-trump">Continue reading...</a>
